title: Graded comparison for filtered bifunctors
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with ordinary cochain derived categories $D(\mathcal A),D(\mathcal B),D(\mathcal C)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and with all localizations and Hom groups taken in a common larger universe. For any of these abelian categories $\mathcal E$, let $DF(\mathcal E)$ be the localization of cochain complexes with decreasing filtrations by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration, def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] at maps that are quasi-isomorphisms on every graded piece. Filtrations are uniformly finite: $F^aK=K$, $F^{b+1}K=0$ for some integers $a\le b$ independent of cochain degree. Write $DF^{[a,b]}$ for the full subcategory whose graded pieces vanish outside $a\le p\le b$, and write $\omega$ and $\operatorname{gr}^p$ for forgetting the filtration and taking the $p$-th grade. Suppose a triangulated bifunctor $G:D(\mathcal A)\times D(\mathcal B)\to D(\mathcal C)$ (respectively $G:D(\mathcal A)^{\mathrm{op}}\times D(\mathcal B)\to D(\mathcal C)$) has a lift $\widetilde G:DF(\mathcal A)\times DF(\mathcal B)\to DF(\mathcal C)$ (respectively $DF(\mathcal A)^{\mathrm{op}}\times DF(\mathcal B)\to DF(\mathcal C)$), exact in each variable, with an isomorphism of bifunctors $\phi_G:\omega\widetilde G\xrightarrow{\sim}G\circ(\omega,\omega)$, and suppose $\widetilde G$ sends $DF^{[a,b]}\times DF^{[c,d]}$ into $DF^{[a+c,b+d]}$ (respectively into $DF^{[-b+c,-a+d]}$). Then $\phi_G$ canonically identifies $\operatorname{gr}^i\widetilde G$ with $\bigoplus_{j+k=i}G(\operatorname{gr}^j,\operatorname{gr}^k)$ (respectively with $\bigoplus_{j+k=i}G(\operatorname{gr}^{-j},\operatorname{gr}^k)$). If $H:G_1\to G_2$ is a natural transformation and $\widetilde H:\widetilde G_1\to\widetilde G_2$ is a filtered lift whose underlying map is identified with $H\circ(\omega,\omega)$ by the two $\phi_{G_i}$, these graded comparisons identify $\operatorname{gr}^i\widetilde H$ with $\bigoplus_{j+k=i}H(\operatorname{gr}^j,\operatorname{gr}^k)$ (respectively $\bigoplus_{j+k=i}H(\operatorname{gr}^{-j},\operatorname{gr}^k)$). If $H$ is an isomorphism of bifunctors, then $\widetilde H$ is an isomorphism. The sums are finite on each pair of finite-filtered inputs. The same assertions apply to bounded or one-sided cochain derived categories, or to full triangulated domains, provided the domains contain the pure graded pieces of their objects and are stable under filtration truncations and the stated bifunctors and lifts take values in the asserted domains. No existence of a lift of an arbitrary ordinary transformation is asserted.

proof.text: Write $M_{\le j}=t_{<j+1}M$, $N_{\le k}=t_{<k+1}N$, and $T_p=t_{\ge p}t_{<p+1}$. These exact functors, their natural maps and triangles, and the exact graded functors are supplied by [lem-trf-filtered-unbounded-truncation]. Fix $j+k=i$. In the covariant case define $Q_{jk}(M,N)=\operatorname{gr}^i\widetilde G(M_{\le j},N_{\le k})$. Apply $\operatorname{gr}^i\widetilde G(M_{\le j},-)$ to $T_kN\to N_{\le k}\to N_{\le k-1}\to$. Its last unshifted term is zero: the interval bound places it in grades $\le j+k-1=i-1$. The zero-cone criterion [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] gives an isomorphism $\operatorname{gr}^i\widetilde G(M_{\le j},T_kN)\to Q_{jk}$. Apply the first-variable functor to $T_jM\to M_{\le j}\to M_{\le j-1}\to$; its discarded output also has grades $\le i-1$. Thus the natural composite $s_{jk}:\operatorname{gr}^i\widetilde G(T_jM,T_kN)\to Q_{jk}$ is invertible. The pure output has only grade $i$; the pure-grade equivalence in the truncation node identifies its $\operatorname{gr}^i$ with $\omega$. Consequently $\alpha_{jk}=\phi_G(T_jM,T_kN)\circ s_{jk}^{-1}$, with those pure-grade identifications, is the natural isomorphism $Q_{jk}\to G(\operatorname{gr}^jM,\operatorname{gr}^kN)$. This comparison concerns the two cutoff inputs, not the original pair.

source.place: proof of Lemma 5.1.4(i), first paragraph, p.40

proof.text: For the contravariant-first case, fix $j+k=i$, put $p=-j$, and instead define $Q_{jk}(M,N)=\operatorname{gr}^i\widetilde G(t_{\ge p}M,N_{\le k})$. The first input has grades $\ge p$ and the second grades $\le k$. In the triangle $T_kN\to N_{\le k}\to N_{\le k-1}\to$, the discarded output has grades $\le -p+k-1=i-1$, so it induces an isomorphism $\operatorname{gr}^i\widetilde G(t_{\ge p}M,T_kN)\to Q_{jk}$. Apply the contravariant first-variable functor to $t_{\ge p+1}M\to t_{\ge p}M\to T_pM\to$. The resulting triangle starts $\widetilde G(T_pM,T_kN)\to\widetilde G(t_{\ge p}M,T_kN)\to\widetilde G(t_{\ge p+1}M,T_kN)\to$; its third term has grades $\le -(p+1)+k=i-1$. Exactness and [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] therefore give an invertible composite $s_{jk}:\operatorname{gr}^i\widetilde G(T_pM,T_kN)\to Q_{jk}$. Its pure output has only grade $-p+k=i$. Define $\alpha_{jk}=\phi_G(T_pM,T_kN)\circ s_{jk}^{-1}$ using the pure-grade identifications, obtaining $Q_{jk}\xrightarrow{\sim}G(\operatorname{gr}^{-j}M,\operatorname{gr}^kN)$. All half-line bounds used here follow by applying the stated finite interval bound to actual finite support intervals of the inputs.

Construct $\beta:\operatorname{gr}^i\widetilde G(M,N)\to\bigoplus_{j+k=i}Q_{jk}(M,N)$ by its components. Covariantly use the quotient maps $M\to M_{\le j}$ and $N\to N_{\le k}$. Contravariantly use the inclusion $t_{\ge -j}M\to M$ (which reverses direction under $\widetilde G$) and $N\to N_{\le k}$. Steps 1 and 2 show $Q_{jk}=0$ unless both corresponding input grades are nonzero. Thus all sums can be taken over finite support intervals. On any finite diagram choose common intervals for its inputs, so the same finite index set is used at every vertex; enlarging it only adds zero summands. Each cutoff map commutes with cochain shifts and with the cone triangles: on complexes it is the termwise inclusion or quotient, and the cone has the direct-sum filtration. Hence $\beta$ is a morphism of distinguished triangles in each variable, before using $\phi_G$ or $\alpha_{jk}$. The target triangles are distinguished by [lem-weil-finite-sums-distinguished-triangles]. For pure inputs of grades $a,b$, all $Q_{jk}$ vanish except possibly $(j,k)=(a,b)$ covariantly and $(-a,b)$ contravariantly. The source also vanishes unless $i=a+b$ or $i=-a+b$, respectively. In the remaining case the cutoff maps are isomorphisms, so $\beta$ is an isomorphism. First fix pure $M$ and induct on the support width of $N$: the triangle $T_dN\to N\to N_{\le d-1}\to$ splits off its highest grade $d$, and [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] applied to $\beta$ proves the middle component invertible from the two shorter cases. Next fix arbitrary $N$ and induct on the support width of $M$ using $T_bM\to M\to M_{\le b-1}\to$; in the contravariant case the image triangle has reversed order, and the same triangle-morphism lemma applies to its two known components. The zero-input case starts both inductions, and width one is the pure case. This proves $\beta$ invertible for all finite-filtered pairs. Define the required comparison $\Theta_G=(\bigoplus\alpha_{jk})\circ\beta$.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.4(i), equation (5.1) and finite-filtration reduction, pp.40–41

proof.text: For a compatible filtered lift $\widetilde H:\widetilde G_1\to\widetilde G_2$, naturality at the cutoff inclusions and quotients gives $\beta_2\circ\operatorname{gr}^i\widetilde H=(\bigoplus\operatorname{gr}^i\widetilde H(\text{cut inputs}))\circ\beta_1$. Naturality at the pure-to-cut maps in Steps 1 and 2 gives $\operatorname{gr}^i\widetilde H(\text{cut inputs})\circ s_{1,jk}=s_{2,jk}\circ\operatorname{gr}^i\widetilde H(\text{pure inputs})$. Multiply by the two inverses $s_{r,jk}^{-1}$ and use the assumed equation $\phi_{G_2}\circ\omega\widetilde H=H(\omega,\omega)\circ\phi_{G_1}$ on the pure pair. It gives $\alpha_{2,jk}\circ\operatorname{gr}^i\widetilde H(\text{cut inputs})=H(\operatorname{gr}^jM,\operatorname{gr}^kN)\circ\alpha_{1,jk}$ covariantly, and the same equation with first grade $-j$ contravariantly. Substituting in the first equality proves $\Theta_{G_2}\circ\operatorname{gr}^i\widetilde H=(\bigoplus H(\operatorname{gr}^jM,\operatorname{gr}^kN))\circ\Theta_{G_1}$, with $j$ replaced by $-j$ in the first slot contravariantly. This checks every component of the finite biproduct square directly; no induction on equality of transformations is needed.

If $H$ is an isomorphism, the finite direct sum in Step 4 is an isomorphism, so every $\operatorname{gr}^i\widetilde H(M,N)$ is invertible. Choose a distinguished cone triangle for this morphism. Exactness of each $\operatorname{gr}^i$ from [lem-trf-filtered-unbounded-truncation] and [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] imply that every graded object of its cone $C$ is zero in $D(\mathcal C)$. Represent $C$ by a finite filtered complex $K$. Each $\operatorname{gr}^iK$ is acyclic, so the chain map $K\to0$ is a filtered quasi-isomorphism by the definition of the localization. Thus $C\cong0$ in $DF(\mathcal C)$, and the zero-cone criterion applied to the original triangle proves $\widetilde H(M,N)$ invertible. The component inverses are natural: multiply the naturality equation for $\widetilde H$ on each side by these inverses. They therefore form the inverse transformation.

The bounded and one-sided variants are reduced to the unbounded statement. By [lem-trf-filtered-bounded-localization-comparison], the natural functors $D^bF$, $D^+F$, $D^-F\to DF$ are fully faithful, also for every fixed filtration interval, with essential images the objects whose graded cohomology is bounded in the corresponding cochain directions. The filtrations, shifts and filtered mapping cones of bounded (resp. bounded-below, bounded-above) complexes are again such complexes, so the inclusion sends cone triangles to cone triangles and identifies each of these categories with a full triangulated subcategory of $DF$. Each such subcategory contains the cut and pure objects of its objects: $F^rK$, $K/F^rK$ and their subquotients preserve any strict cochain-degree bound on a representative, so the truncation functors and triangles of [lem-trf-filtered-unbounded-truncation] restrict to it. The induction is on finite filtration width, not cochain degree. Hence these variants are instances of the full-domain case. For the stated full triangulated domains, the assumed closure puts each cut and pure object used in Steps 1–4 inside the domain; triangulatedness gives its cone triangles and finite sums, and the range assumptions put every bifunctor value there. Fullness retains the constructed maps and their inverses; the Step 5 cone is zero in the ambient localization and hence in the full domain. These observations establish all restricted assertions under exactly the closure and range hypotheses in the statement. Throughout, a filtered transformation is given; no construction of a lift of an arbitrary ordinary transformation is used.
